title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-13
notes:
West leads the ♦K against 4♥. South has a certain loser in spades, diamonds, and clubs. South must avoid losing a second diamond trick. As West has shown 6 diamonds with his weak 2 bid, East is likely to have at least 3 hearts. Trying to ruff a diamond in dummy is unlikely to work.

South's best chance to make the contract is with a loser-on-loser play. South can easily succeed by winning the diamond lead and exiting a diamond. If West returns another diamond, South can discard a spade from the dummy (a loser-on-loser play). If West had not continued diamonds, South would have executed the loser-on-loser play himself after gaining the lead.

South has now effectively traded a possible diamond ruff, that East could overruff, for a safer spade ruff. West's club shift is won with the ♣A. In case West was dealt 2 hearts and only 1 or 2 spades, South should take the precaution of drawing 2 rounds of trumps before taking his spade ruff.
